LibTmux.Server

Description

Observe an existing tmux daemon through an owned Server handle.

A Server represents one adoption of one endpoint. withServer owns its socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers. Closing this scope releases those resources; it does not send kill-server. The tmux noun Client refers to detached observations in LibTmux.Snapshot. withRuntime and withServerIn give several handles shared resource limits and independent Server scopes.

capture returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic transaction over tmux and operating-system state.

Operational failures use TmuxException. tryTmux catches that type only. Cancellation retains its original exception class. If bounded cleanup cannot finish, cleanupRecoveries retrieves the owning recovery scope from the exception context. A failed callback remains the primary failure.

Open and observe

data Server Source #

One pinned endpoint and connection generation. The constructor is hidden. Retaining this value after withServer or withServerIn keeps no admission open.

data ServerConfig Source #

Pure configuration, checked when withServer or withServerIn opens the handle. Paths retain POSIX bytes; no text decoding or shell interpretation occurs.

serverConfig :: PosixPath -> ServerConfig Source #

Configure an existing socket, resolving tmux through PATH when opened. The private pin uses the socket's parent directory. The capture timeout is two seconds; callers can change it before opening a Server scope.

withServer :: ServerConfig -> (Server -> IO a) -> IO a Source #

Open one handle, run the callback, then perform bounded owned cleanup. Cleanup never replaces a callback exception. Incomplete cleanup raises CleanupFailed after success, or annotates the original callback failure with a reachable CleanupRecovery. No daemon shutdown is requested.

capture :: Server -> IO Snapshot Source #

Acquire the complete baseline graph, metadata and attached clients. Returned values own their data and remain usable after withServer exits. Capacity and acquisition failure are errors; they never become empty lists.

serverGeneration :: Server -> Generation Source #

The handle's opaque generation, available without contacting tmux.

Shared ownership

data Runtime Source #

Shared resource limits and cleanup ownership for Server handles. Create one with withRuntime, then adopt endpoints through withServerIn. Detached Snapshot values retain no Runtime.

withRuntime :: (Runtime -> IO a) -> IO a Source #

Own a Runtime for the callback and perform bounded cleanup afterward. Closing it retires every adopted handle; application-owned threads remain the application's responsibility. Late adoption fails with RuntimeClosed. The daemon remains running.

Callback failures and cancellation keep their original exception class. Incomplete cleanup retains a CleanupRecovery in the exception context; use tryTmux and cleanupRecoveries to keep that responsibility reachable.

withServerIn :: Runtime -> ServerConfig -> (Server -> IO a) -> IO a Source #

Adopt one endpoint within an existing Runtime and close only that handle after the callback. Other handles remain admitted under the shared limits; each adoption has its own serverGeneration. Use withServer for one handle.

Failed adoption can retain a CleanupRecovery before a Server exists. Inspection, retry and waiting through that owner stay scoped to the failed adoption. Cleanup preserves application exceptions, incoming masking state and cancellation; known acquisition failures use TmuxException.

Operational failures

data TmuxException Source #

Library operational failures. Context-preserving catching retains any cleanup owners; the original application or cancellation exception keeps its class when the callback itself failed.

Constructors

ServerClosed

Admission through the retained Server handle has closed.

RuntimeClosed

Admission through the retained Runtime has closed.

InvalidConfiguration !Text

Configuration failed before acquisition.

InvalidObservation !Text

Acquired metadata failed final validation.

OperationFailed !SomeException

Known backend failure with its original cause.

CleanupFailed !CleanupStatus !(Maybe SomeException)

Cleanup remained incomplete or its worker could not start.

data CleanupStatus Source #

Local observations of the selected physical and logical responsibility. Each inspection returns new metadata; it performs no tmux operation.

cleanupRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CleanupRecovery] Source #

Cleanup owners retained by a failed or cancelled scope. The context comes from tryTmux or tryWithContext. Inspection performs no tmux IO. Nested scopes can contribute overlapping owners; inspect and resume each retained responsibility through inspectCleanup and resumeCleanup.

cleanupFailure :: CleanupRecovery -> Maybe SomeException Source #

Exception that interrupted the original cleanup attempt, when there was one. Pending ownership alone need not have an associated exception.

cleanupObservation :: CleanupRecovery -> CleanupStatus Source #

The cleanup metadata recorded when this recovery owner was attached.

inspectCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus Source #

Inspect current owned cleanup and logical uncertainty without tmux IO.

resumeCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus Source #

Retry bounded owned cleanup. An incomplete result retains this owner; the operation does not retry a tmux command or release logical uncertainty.

awaitCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus Source #

Wait for this target's physical cleanup, then inspect its logical debt. The wait has no deadline. Cancellation or failure preserves an annotated cleanup owner. Use resumeCleanup when the caller requires a bounded attempt.

detachUnresolved :: CleanupRecovery -> Operation -> IO Bool Source #

Relinquish one logical operation from this cleanup scope. This releases no native resources and does not prove that daemon-side work completed.

Correlated capture recovery

data CaptureRecovery Source #

A reachable owner for one failed or cancelled capture. The receipt holds metadata only; the Runtime retains any remaining native and logical owners.

data Outcome Source #

First caller result. Later evidence can retire responsibility without rewriting OutcomeUnknown or ConnectionRetired.

Constructors

Succeeded

Validated successful response and completion proof.

Failed

Validated command failure.

NotDispatched

Proof that the operation was never dispatched.

Dispatch may have happened; completion remains uncertain.

The connection retired while responsibility remained.
